4. Mr. Shahabuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that by refusing the injunction by the Courts below the very purpose and intent of the Family Courts Ordinance has been frustrated. He submits that if opposite party No. 1 is given in marriage elsewhere and if the suit is decreed it will create complications and for that matter the Courts below ought to have granted the injunction prayed for. He further argued that the trial Court committed illegality in examining opposite party No. 1 before the hearing of the injunction matter and also before the filing of the written statement. He submits that there is no provision in the Family Courts Ordinance to examine a party before filing of the written statement. He also submits that the Courts below violated the provision of Section 13 of the Family Courts Ordinance by refusing to grant injunction. He also argued that the appellate Court also committed illegality in holding that the provision of Order 39 Rule 1 of the Code is not applicable in a proceeding under Family Courts Ordinance. He submits that there is no specific bar in granting injunction and the Family Court can act under the provision of section 141 of the Code for giving adequate relief which is required to be given to a party under Family Courts Ordinance when there is no specific provision in the Ordinance as regards injunction. He argued that the whole purpose of the suit will be frustrated if the injunction prayed for be not granted. 

 6. Admittedly opposite party No. 1 was married to the petitioner and their marriage was duly registered. The case of the petitioner is that opposite party Nos. 2-5 are keeping opposite party No.1 in their house and not allowing her to come to the domain of the petitioner and for that he had to file this suit in the Family Court for restitution of his conjugal right and during the pendency of the suit he prayed for injunction under Order 39 Rule 1 of the Code. The learned Subordinate Judge while disposing of the appeal found that this provision of the Code is not applicable in a case filed under the Family Courts Ordinance. The learned Advocate for the petitioner argued that if during the pendency of the suit opposite party 1 is given in marriage elsewhere and if the suit is decreed then there will arise complications and for avoiding those complications the injunction prayed for ought to have been granted. He argued that the whole purpose of the suit will be frustrated if the injunction is not granted. Admittedly the suit was filed under Family Courts Ordinance at Ramgonj. I have carefully gone through the provision of Family Courts Ordinance, 1985. Under this Ordinance all the Munsif  are to act as judges of the Family Courts and Section 5 of the Family Courts Ordinance provided the jurisdiction of the Court and it also provided that a Family Court shall have exclusive jurisdiction to entertain, try and dispose of any suit relating to or arising out of all or any of the following matters namely:- 

 12. The learned Advocate then placed before this Court a decision reported in 23 DLR (SC) 81 (Naeem Finance Ltd. Vs. Bashir Ahmed Rafiquo) where it has been held that in the absence of any rules made by the High Court, Section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure will be applicable and enquiries and other proceedings contemplated under it will be held as far as possible according to the provisions of the Civil Procedure Code. Relying on this decision the learned Advocate submits that where the law maker has not made any provision as regards injunction in a Family Court this Court or the Family Court may Act under section 141 of the Code and grant the desired relief invoking the provision of Order 39, Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure. But 'this decision of our Supreme Court is not applicable to the present case as in the Family Courts Ordinance clear provision has been made for institution of suit, issuance of summons, filing of written statement, pre-trial hearing, hearing, execution of the decree etc. This means the Ordinance is a self-contained Ordinance. This law is a special law and it provided. the procedure to be followed by the Courts in proceeding with the suits that may be filed under the Ordinance. In such circumstances it cannot be found that the provision provided under Section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure can be attracted in the present case. In that view of the matter I hold that this decision of our Supreme Court has no manner of application to the present case. It may be argued that if the provision for injunction as prayed for in the present case is not given the whole purpose of the suit filed for restitution of conjugal life will be frustrated. But where the law-makers have not incorporated such a provision in the Ordinance for the reasons best known to them the Court by way of interpretation cannot incorporate anything which the law makers have specifically avoided to incorporate.
